description.narrative:
The programme is a continuation of the accompaniment program initiated in 2004 with the Angolan Bishops Conference and its Peace and Justice Commission (ANG090) which produced significant results (see external evaluation and final progress in implementation report). The current programme consists of two interdependent projects. The project proposal submitted by the Angolan Bishop’s Peace and Justice Commission entitled Por uma Justiça Economica, adopting the title of the 2006 Pastoral Letter of the Bishops Conference for Angola and Sao Tome (CEAST) and the Economic Justice Accompaniment Project hosted by CRS Angola Trocaire, as the second Caritas/CIDSE working group member with a permanent representation in Angola, facilitates the collection and transfer of funds from the remaining European partners (Cafod, Cordaid, Misereor and Secours Catholique).
The programme has three pillars: research, social monitoring and advocacy/networking. It furthermore has a specific focus on capacity building / sustainability. The thematic focus of the project is on promoting economic justice broadly defined as egalitarian, efficient, transparent and participatory socio-economic development. The focus is predominantly on the country’s extractive industries (mainly oil and diamonds) and the national budget process. The three pillars are interlinked in the sense that the Church wants to establish a strong knowledgebase in order to be able to advocate effectively around issues that are considered sensitive in the Angolan context. The social monitoring pillar is meant to bring socio-economic justice issues to the grassroots level in dioceses and parishes as the specific research and advocacy agenda will be more focused at the national and international levels due to the highly centralized nature of government decision-making.
Concepts such as research based advocacy, policy analysis and social monitoring are new for the Church in Angola and skilled accompaniment is needed to build up capacity of the partner to fully master these techniques. The accompaniment is based on a learning-by-doing approach.
